concepts.title: Sensory Processes and the Nature of Stimuli
concepts.definition: Knowing the world begins with sensory processes: receptors in eyes, ears, skin, nose and mouth convert physical energy -- light, sound, pressure, molecules -- into neural signals. Each sense responds to its own stimulus within limits of intensity, so the world we register is only the band our receptors can catch.
concepts.key_idea: Senses are translators -- physical energy in, neural code out -- and each translates only its own band.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy104.txt sensory sections (nature of sensory processes, receptors, stimuli, modalities of sense)
question_patterns: what are sensory processes in psychology
in class 11 sensory attentional and perceptual processes: how do receptors convert stimuli
why can humans not see all light that exists
list the senses and their stimuli
distinguish stimulus from sensation with an example
what happens when a receptor is stimulated below its threshold

solution_steps.explain: Each sense answers a specific physical energy -- light for vision, sound waves for hearing, molecules for smell and taste.
Receptors convert that energy into neural impulses the brain can read.
Intensities below threshold go unregistered, so sensation already selects from reality.

concepts.title: Attention: Selectivity and Its Determinants
concepts.definition: Attention selects a few stimuli for full processing and screens out the rest -- a spotlight with narrow beams. Its focus is driven both by stimulus properties (intensity, novelty, movement, contrast) and by personal factors (motive, interest, expectation), which is why the same lecture holds one student and bores another.
concepts.key_idea: Attention is a bouncer at the door of mind -- stimuli loud, new or interesting get in; the rest wait outside.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy104.txt attention sections (processes and types of attention, determinants of attention, selectivity, span of attention)
question_patterns: define attention and explain its selective nature
in class 11 sensory attentional and perceptual processes: what stimulus factors attract attention
how do interest and motive direct attention
explain attention span with an example
why do we fail to notice events outside our attention

solution_steps.explain: Capacity is limited, so consciousness receives a selection, not the full stream.
Intensity, novelty, movement and contrast pull attention from outside; motives, interest and expectations pull from inside.
Attention may be focused on one task or divided among several, with cost rising as division increases.

concepts.title: Perception: Organisation of Sensation into Meaning
concepts.definition: Perception turns sensations into meaningful wholes: figures against grounds, grouped elements, completed outlines and depth read from cues. It is shaped by learning and motivation -- the same ambiguous drawing becomes a duck or a rabbit depending on the perceiver -- so perception is a construction, not a photograph.
concepts.key_idea: Perception is the mind's rendering -- sensations are raw pixels; meaning is drawn in by the perceiver.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy104.txt perception sections (form and space perception, figure ground, grouping, depth perception, principles of perceptual organisation, perceptual constancy)
question_patterns: distinguish sensation from perception with an example
in class 11 sensory attentional and perceptual processes: explain figure ground organisation
how do we perceive depth with two eyes
what is perceptual constancy give examples
how do needs and expectations shape perception
explain the gestalt principles of perceptual grouping

solution_steps.explain: The perceptual system splits the field into a focused figure against a receding ground.
Elements near each other, similar, or moving together group into wholes; gaps get filled in.
Cues from both eyes and from motion give depth; past experience and motives give objects their meaning and stability.

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a noisy fair, a mother instantly hears her child's voice calling from far away. Explain this using the determinants of attention.

solution_template.explain: The child's voice is supremely significant to the mother -- a motivational determinant.
Louder but less meaningful voices fail to capture her the same way.
Attention follows significance as well as loudness -- inner determinants can beat outer intensity.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A friend reads an ambiguous drawing as a young woman; you see an old woman. Explain the difference using perceptual processes.

solution_template.explain: The ink pattern reaching both retinas is identical -- sensation is the same.
Each mind groups lines into a different figure -- organisation is constructive.
Experience and expectation complete the drawing differently -- perception is interpretation, not copying.
